Visit note | 2025-04-05 12:30 PM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Jui Patwary, 53, female. Mrs. Patwary attends for review regarding her feet, reporting ongoing numbness in her toes, a tingling sensation like pins and needles, and a persistent burning discomfort in both feet. She works as a bus driver, and these symptoms started after years of high sugar found at a health camp in Badda. She has a history of Bronchial asthma. She reports taking her diabetes medications regularly and denies any recent falls, chest pain, or shortness of breath. On examination: reduced sensation at 6 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 124/82 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 83 kg. Lower limb reflexes are sluggish but symmetric. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: a prescription was issued for her nerve symptoms. She was advised to check her feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep her blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-04-05 03:30 PM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Hafsa Pramanik, 42, female. Ms. Pramanik comes in today reporting brittle nails, looking visibly pale, and experiencing shortness of breath when climbing stairs. She works as a pharmacist and notes that her tiredness worsened after a long spell of poor meals while living alone in Savar. She has no known comorbid conditions and denies any recent fever, chest pain, or digestive bleeding. On examination: haemoglobin 10.4 g/dL, BP 127/86 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 55 kg. Conjunctivae are pale, and chest and heart examinations are unremarkable. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

Visit note | 2025-04-05 03:30 PM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Bilkis Islam, 76, female. Mrs. Islam presents with complaints of producing more sputum than usual, breathlessness that has been worse for several days, and a long history of smoking. She is a homemaker, and her breathing trouble worsened after catching a cold at a crowded market in Sirajganj. She has a known comorbidity of Essential hypertension. She denies any chest pain or severe dizziness. On examination: SpO2 89%, BP 151/96 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, weight 53 kg. Auscultation reveals widespread wheezing and reduced breath sounds. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-04-05 03:30 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Mita Ghosh, 55, female. Mrs. Ghosh reports suffering from a creaking knee and stiffness in the morning that lasts for a few minutes. She works as a tailor, and her joint discomfort has been worse since moving to a building with no lift in Bogura. She has no chronic comorbidities and denies any recent joint trauma, locking, or sudden swelling. On examination: BMI 31.8, BP 127/84 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 90 kg. Visit note | 2025-04-05 04:00 PM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Lamia Bepari, 39, female. She denies any flank pain or vomiting. On examination: temperature 99.8°F, BP 116/83 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 63 kg. Abdominal examination reveals mild suprapubic tenderness without guarding. Follow-up in 1 week if symptoms continue.

Visit note | 2025-04-05 04:30 PM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Jahid Howlader, 53, male. Mr. Howlader attends for review, describing breathlessness on effort and a heavy feeling in the chest that eases with rest within minutes, along with chest tightness when walking fast or climbing. He works as a tailor and first noticed these symptoms while climbing to a fourth-floor flat in Rampura. He has no reported chronic comorbidities. Interestingly, he presents with jaw and left arm discomfort on effort with no chest pain. He denies palpitations or nocturnal symptoms. On examination: BP 158/85 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 87 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no murmurs, and lung fields are clear. Assessment: Stable angina. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid heavy exertion until review, walk 20 minutes daily on flat ground, and stop smoking. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and fasting lipid profile.
